gaps.sentence: The colonel ___ his soldiers to advance at dawn.
gaps.explanation: Order + object + to-infinitive reports a command; suggest and hope do not take object + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I didn't take your charger,' she insisted. She ___ taking my charger.
gaps.explanation: Denials are reported as deny + -ing: denied taking.

gaps.sentence: 'Where are you going?' she asked her brother. She asked her brother where he ___ going.
gaps.explanation: are you going → he was going: statement order with backshifted continuous.

gaps.sentence: 'The road is being resurfaced,' the council said. The council said the road ___ resurfaced.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive (is being resurfaced) backshifts to past continuous passive: was being resurfaced.

gaps.sentence: 'It was me who ate the last biscuit,' the boy admitted. The boy ___ eating the last biscuit.
gaps.explanation: Admit takes a gerund (admit doing) or admit that + clause — never admit to do.

gaps.sentence: 'Why did you cancel the order?' he asked. He asked why I ___ the order.
gaps.explanation: Wh-questions keep the wh-word but drop do-support and backshift: did you cancel → I had cancelled.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm sorry I forgot the meeting,' she said. She ___ forgetting the meeting.
gaps.explanation: An apology is reported with 'apologised for + gerund'.

gaps.sentence: 'I've been studying all night,' she said. She said she ___ studying all night.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been + -ing backshifts to had been + -ing.
